observation.visible_scene: A tight, eye-level close-up of a painted metal railing/grille fixed above a pale ledge. Centered on the ledge, in front of the railing, sits a small translucent dome-shaped blob with a thin glossy film spreading at its base. The background is heavily out of focus: dark green foliage with bright circular bokeh on the left and a soft pinkish wall on the right. A vertical bar of the railing crosses the upper middle, and a thicker post with a flared base stands to the right of the blob.
visible_changes: The overall composition is essentially static throughout the excerpt: the horizontal railing bar, the vertical bar, the right post, and the dome-shaped blob hold the same positions relative to the frame edges from the first to the last sample (blob center stays around the same x/y on the ledge), showing no translation of the subject.

The blob's shape and size do not visibly grow, shrink, slide, or vanish; only its surface highlight and the thin liquid film at its base look marginally different between frames, which is too subtle to confirm as melting, spreading, or any other process.

The out-of-focus background highlights (bokeh) flicker and shift slightly in shape and brightness from frame to frame, while the railing and ledge remain fixed, indicating the change is in the blurred background rather than a camera move across the scene.
No dripping, contact, or motion of the railing or the blob is observed; the flare at the base of the right post is a static feature, not an active drip.
outside_clip_unknowns: The material identity of the blob (e.g., ice, resin, a droplet mass) and whether it is mid-melt or stable.
Whether any slow change to the blob or background motion began before or continues after the crop boundaries.
The cause of the background bokeh flicker (moving leaves/wind vs. lighting or focus changes).
uncertain_details: Whether the slight difference in the blob's gloss/outline across frames is a real physical change or just lighting/reflection variation.
Whether there is any negligible camera drift versus a perfectly locked-off shot; the railing's position is constant enough that camera motion cannot be confirmed.

the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
